about.what: Which robot hangs in which slot of the frame, as of October 2026 (decided 2026-10-02: arms are named by slot; the old prime-number robot ids live on only here). Read by the robot side (robot/), never by the planning code: aris/rig.py does not read site/.
about.slots_note: slot = row 1..3 along table y (-1.21, 0, +1.21 m) and L/R by table x (-0.305 / +0.305); see config/rig.json slots.
about.mapping_source: the orchestrator's brief, 2026-10-02: 13 -> 1L, 17 -> 1R, 31 -> 2L, 71 -> 2R, 2 -> 3L, 97 -> 3R. The ids were permuted on the hardware once already; verify every row with `aris-robot identify` before a run.
about.ip_source: robot/site.json `arms` (control-stack briefing 2026-09-09, section 5, arm_registry.py), carried over by robot id. The DDS domain there was the robot id; it is copied as `domain`.
about.live_note: on 2026-10-02 the arms under control are 2R and 3R (config/two_arms). 2L has no arm hanging (its hanger is steel only).
about.sure_note: `sure: false` marks a row nobody has checked against the hardware since the permutation; the reason is in `why`.

1L.why: not checked since the permutation; arm not under control

1R.why: not checked since the permutation; arm not under control

2L.why: the 2026-10-02 brief says no arm hangs in 2L today; where robot 31 is now is not known here

2R.why: live today, but robot 71 had no IP on 2026-09-15 (HARDWARE_DAY1 1.6); the address .14 is the briefing's, confirm it

3L.why: not checked since the permutation; whether a robot hangs here (switched off) is not known here

3R.why: live today; address from the briefing, confirm with `aris-robot identify`
